assessment.summary: BTK (Q06187) is an exceptionally well-validated drug target with six approved small-molecule inhibitors, over 21,000 ChEMBL IC50 entries, and multiple ultra-high-resolution co-crystal structures. The target has strong disease validation across B-cell malignancies and immunological conditions, with active ongoing research into next-generation covalent, non-covalent, and PROTAC-based approaches.
evidence_gaps: Resistance mechanisms to approved covalent BTK inhibitors (e.g., C481S mutation) limit utility of existing drugs, and full structural characterisation of all clinically relevant resistance mutants may be incomplete
Long-term safety and efficacy data for newer non-covalent inhibitors (e.g., pirtobrutinib) in broader patient populations are still emerging
Selectivity profiles across the full kinome for many chemical series may not be fully characterised, particularly for novel PROTAC degraders
Biomarker strategies for patient stratification and predicting BTK inhibitor-associated immune modulation remain under investigation
